C-RELEASE-CASK-SIGNED-DIGEST.Summary: The release workflow's Homebrew cask handoff resolves its sha256 only from the signed macOS release artifact: the publish-cask job downloads exactly mark-macos-arm64-release by name into its own path instead of every run artifact, addresses the Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg.sha256 sidecar by that explicit artifact path with no find/head selection over the staged tree, and fails closed before any cask mutation when a fresh hash of the signed DMG beside the sidecar disagrees with it ([ReleaseCask][publish-cask][BLOCK_RELEASE_CASK_DIGEST_MISMATCH]); the value written into the cask stays the sidecar value per B2CR-3 — the hash is only a coherence check.
C-RELEASE-CASK-SIGNED-DIGEST.Problem: Defect confirmed directly against this tree (release.yml VERSION 3.9.0, HEAD bb68fd6c, 2026-11-22): the publish-cask job (:1575) downloads ALL run artifacts with actions/download-artifact@v4 and no pattern/name (:1598-1601 — the step declares only path: /tmp/release-stage, and artifact v4 unpacks each artifact into its own subdirectory), then picks the Homebrew cask digest with an unconstrained selection, SHA256_FILE=$(find /tmp/release-stage -name "Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg.sha256" | head -1) (:1633). Since C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT (#315, commit 3f61c2b7, merged 2026-11-22; the pre-split tree at bec319f3 carries no -staged artifact) a stable run carries that sidecar filename in THREE artifacts holding TWO different values: mark-macos-arm64-release-staged carries the digest of the UNSIGNED staged DMG (written by the build job's stage step, shasum -a 256 "$DMG_DST" | awk '{print $1}' > "$DMG_DST.sha256", :725, and re-emitted for the remaining staged files in the loop at :736-741, uploaded :889-900); mark-macos-arm64-release carries the fresh digest of the SIGNED DMG re-emitted by the sign job (:1162-1166, uploaded :1260-1274); and the publication inventory bundle release-publication-${TAG} carries a copy of the signed digest (assembled by prepare-publication's inventory list, :1355, hashed into publication.sha256 :1437, uploaded :1439-1448). find | head -1 over the all-artifact tree can therefore hand the cask the digest of a DMG that is never published, in a filesystem-order-dependent way, and nothing downstream re-checks the written value: the idempotent exact-PR comparison (:1675-1676) and the tap-side required check validate the PR against whatever value was chosen, not against the published asset. The Homebrew cask is a public trust boundary — it pins what `brew upgrade` installs — so a wrong digest there converts a correct release into a broken or spoofable install.
C-RELEASE-CASK-SIGNED-DIGEST.Relationship: The defect originates in C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT: that change created the mark-macos-arm64-release-staged handoff artifact carrying a second, different value under the same sidecar filename, while publish-cask — explicitly left out of its scope (its NonGoal: "no changes to ... the Homebrew cask handoff (publish-cask)") — kept its pre-split all-artifact download and unconstrained find | head -1 selection, which was unambiguous before the split. This change stands on the v3.9.0 boundary C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT established and must preserve it: the unsigned-build/digest-verified-sign chain, the BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH verify-then-sign step, the prepare-publication needs chain and the prerelease-lane equivalence stay untouched. The other consumers of /tmp/release-stage were audited against the same ambiguity and need no change (verified against this tree): prepare-publication downloads with pattern: mark-*-release (:1306), which cannot match the -staged artifact names, and its assemble-exact-asset-inventory step guards every copy on exactly one match — copy_one fails closed with "expected exactly one $NAME" unless the find over /tmp/release-stage returns exactly one file (:1347-1352) — so its Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg.sha256 asset is the signed sidecar by construction; the compose-deterministic-updater-feed find over latest-platform.json (:1328) consumes every match intentionally (a platform-fragment merge with a non-empty guard) rather than selecting one by head, and no -staged artifact contains a fragment. Both stay as they are; only publish-cask has the defect shape (unconstrained selection of one match from many).

Goals.Goal: Explicit signed-artifact selection (owner decision 1): the publish-cask download step names the artifact explicitly — name: mark-macos-arm64-release with its own path, path: /tmp/release-stage/mark-macos-arm64-release — replacing the all-artifact download. The job is provably free of other /tmp/release-stage consumers (verified against this tree): its only staged-tree read is the cask digest sidecar (:1633); the tap is cloned to /tmp/tap (:1646), the cask is edited there, and no other step touches /tmp/release-stage — so the narrowed single-artifact download loses nothing. The unconstrained find … | head -1 selection of a sha256 sidecar disappears from the workflow: the sidecar and the signed DMG beside it are addressed by their explicit artifact-subdirectory paths, CASK_SIDECAR="/tmp/release-stage/mark-macos-arm64-release/Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg.sha256" and SIGNED_DMG="/tmp/release-stage/mark-macos-arm64-release/Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg", with a fail-closed existence check for both files. The pinned action digest of download-artifact and every other step of the job (App-secret gate, token mint, clone, idempotent exact-PR handling, sed-based bump, auto-merge) keep their current shape.

Fail-closed coherence check before the cask is written (owner decision 2): after reading the sidecar value, the job recomputes the SHA-256 of the signed DMG sitting beside it (sha256sum, the established ubuntu-latest digest tool in this workflow — publish uses sha256sum -c, prepare-publication hashes the inventory with sha256sum) and exits nonzero with the marker ::error::[ReleaseCask][publish-cask][BLOCK_RELEASE_CASK_DIGEST_MISMATCH] naming both digests if they disagree — before gh auth setup-git, the tap clone, and any cask mutation. The marker matches the workflow's existing [ReleaseArea][job][BLOCK_REASON] style ([ReleaseAuthorize][authorize-tag][BLOCK_PRERELEASE_CHECKS_NOT_GREEN] :226, [ReleaseSign][sign][BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH] :991-1009, [ReleasePublish][publish][BLOCK_RELEASE_LATEST_ADVANCED] :1573). No status-swallowing construct surrounds the comparison. The value written into the cask is still the sidecar value: the workflow comment "Pull the .sha256 sidecar value (NOT recompute) per B2CR-3." stays, the coherence hash is used only for the comparison and never substituted into the cask, and the existing sed write of "$SHA256" (:1690) is unchanged.

Source-pinned structure and docs (owner decisions 4-5): tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js gains a comment-blind red-control validator, assertCaskSignedDigest(source), mirroring the assertGitleaksChecksumContract / assertPublicationNeedsChain precedent (in-memory source mutations only, no network, no tracked-file edits, CRLF-tolerant \r?\n regexes because Windows checkouts carry \r\n), plus two tests: a positive pin test asserting the named download, the explicit sidecar/DMG paths, the absent find selection, the coherence check with the marker and the retained B2CR-3 policy, and a red-control test mutating the workflow text in memory — restoring the broad unnamed download, removing the coherence check, and reintroducing an unconstrained find | head -1 selection — each asserting the validator throws with its distinct expectation. docs/release-process.md gains one or two sentences in the 4b signing-boundary section stating that the Homebrew cask digest comes only from the signed set and is coherence-checked against the signed DMG before the pull request opens.

GRACE bookkeeping synchronized (owner decision 6): release.yml's own markup gains the version bump 3.9.0 → 3.10.0, a dated C-RELEASE-CASK-SIGNED-DIGEST CHANGE_SUMMARY line, and a publish-cask MODULE_MAP entry naming the signed-only resolution; the test file's contract markup bumps 2.4.0 → 2.5.0 with its own dated entry and validator map line; .grace/graph/features.xml M-046 gains one dated SummaryDelta (placed after the C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT delta, :2397); .grace/verification/features.xml V-M-046 gains the next sequential scenario (scenario-40, after scenario-39 :2561) naming the marker and the focused commands.

Constraints.Constraint: ObservedWriteScope: .github/workflows/release.yml (publish-cask job steps and its MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY markup only); tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js (new validator, two tests, markup); docs/release-process.md (the 4b section's cask sentences only); .grace/graph/features.xml (M-046 SummaryDelta); .grace/verification/features.xml (V-M-046 scenario-40). No renderer or Rust product code, no new workflow files, no npm dependency changes, no new secrets, and no change to the release-cask environment's definition or reviewers.

Every other job and byte of behavior stays as it is: authorize-tag, manual-build, build, sign, prepare-publication and publish are untouched (prepare-publication's exactly-one copy_one guard and pattern-based download are audited and correct — Relationship); artifact names, upload shapes and the pinned action digests stay unchanged; publish-cask keeps needs: [authorize-tag, build, publish], its if: needs.authorize-tag.outputs.prerelease != 'true' skip, environment: release-cask, permissions contents: read, the App-secret gate and token mint, the idempotent exact-PR handling, the cask URL template check, and the required-check-gated auto-merge.

The B2CR-3 policy is preserved verbatim: the cask sha256 is the sidecar value, never a recomputed digest; the coherence hash exists only to refuse a incoherent sidecar/DMG pair and is fail-closed (nonzero exit, marker, no || true, no if-without-exit) and runs before any cask mutation.

The edit is actionlint-clean; the governance suite's existing pins (boundary guard, needs chain, prerelease equivalence, workflow-wide sign concentration, gitleaks contract, beta-checks gate) keep passing unweakened; new red controls mutate only the in-memory source string with CRLF-tolerant regexes.

GRACE bookkeeping is synchronized and release.yml remains the privileged release lane — every edit, including comments, rides the governed process (grace lint current → target → final), and documentation comments are not mixed with digest-selection changes in the same breath.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No changes to the sign job, the build job, prepare-publication or publish; no new artifact names, no upload/download shape changes outside the publish-cask step, no action version or digest changes.

No changes to the cask formula content beyond the digest source: the URL template Mark_#{version}_aarch64.dmg, the alpha/stable cask selection, the PR identity checks, the body text and the auto-merge stay byte-identical; no Windows cask lane is added.

No recompute policy change: the cask never carries a CI-recomputed digest; the B2CR-3 sidecar-sourcing stance and its comment stay. No coherence check is added to prepare-publication or publish — their exactly-one inventory guard and bundle-digest verification already fail closed.
No prerelease-lane change: publish-cask's skip stays exact, and no prerelease tag ever reaches the cask handoff.

No live tag dispatch, cask PR merge, tap-side validation or publication is authorized or performed by this change; the first stable tag run through the narrowed handoff is live evidence recorded in the change bundle after merge.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Selection pin (unit): the governance test asserts on the publishCaskJob slice that the download step is named "download signed macOS release artifacts" and declares exactly name: mark-macos-arm64-release with path: /tmp/release-stage/mark-macos-arm64-release; that the cask PR step addresses the sidecar and the signed DMG by the explicit artifact paths (CASK_SIDECAR=".../Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg.sha256", SIGNED_DMG=".../Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg") with a fail-closed existence check; that no unconstrained find over /tmp/release-stage selecting a sha256 sidecar remains in the job; and that the B2CR-3 comment and the sed write of the sidecar value stay.

Coherence pin (unit): the job recomputes sha256sum over SIGNED_DMG, compares it with the sidecar value, and exits nonzero with ::error::[ReleaseCask][publish-cask][BLOCK_RELEASE_CASK_DIGEST_MISMATCH] naming both digests on mismatch — before gh auth setup-git and any cask mutation — with no status-swallowing construct around the comparison; the positive test pins this ordering (check-then-mutate).

Red controls (unit): assertCaskSignedDigest(source) — comment-blind, in-memory mutations only, CRLF-tolerant \r?\n regexes — rejects each with a distinct expectation: the named download step reverted to the broad unnamed path-only download; the coherence check or its marker removed; the explicit sidecar address replaced by an unconstrained find /tmp/release-stage -name "Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg.sha256" | head -1 selection; and a status-swallowing construct around the digest comparison. The two new tests run green on the checked-in workflow and every existing test in the file stays unweakened.

Docs: docs/release-process.md section 4b carries one or two sentences stating the Homebrew cask digest comes only from the signed macOS release artifact (never the unsigned staged copy) and is coherence-checked against the signed DMG before the pull request opens; no other section, heading or wording changes.

GRACE bookkeeping is synchronized and the focused verification is green: release.yml VERSION 3.10.0 with the dated CHANGE_SUMMARY line and the publish-cask MODULE_MAP entry; the test file VERSION 2.5.0 with the validator in its MODULE_MAP and a dated CHANGE_SUMMARY entry; one dated M-046 SummaryDelta in .grace/graph/features.xml; scenario-40 in .grace/verification/features.xml V-M-046; actionlint clean on release.yml; and the governance plus action-reference tests pass with the new pins.

AffectedAreas.File: docs/release-process.md (4b signing-boundary section, cask sentences only)

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: grace lint --path . --assertions current && grace status --path . --with modules --json
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Green structural pins with red-control evidence: the publish-cask download narrowed to the named signed artifact, the sidecar addressed by its explicit path with the unconstrained find gone, the coherence check failing closed on BLOCK_RELEASE_CASK_DIGEST_MISMATCH before any cask mutation, and the three in-memory mutations each rejected; a workflow diff limited to the publish-cask job and its markup, the test additions, the docs sentences and the graph/verification deltas; actionlint clean. Live evidence stays external: the first stable tag run through the narrowed handoff — cask PR carrying the digest of the published signed DMG — is recorded in the change bundle after merge; a forced digest-mismatch refusal is not inducible on a production tag without publishing a wrong sidecar, so the fail-closed branch's refusal evidence is the unit red controls plus the workflow's own exit-on-mismatch construction, stated explicitly in the bundle rather than discharged by a live fault injection.

Assumptions.Assumption: actions/download-artifact@v4 with an explicit name: merges the artifact's files directly into the declared path (documented v4 behavior; the sign job already relies on the name+path form at :966-970), so /tmp/release-stage/mark-macos-arm64-release/Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg(.sha256) are deterministic paths on every run where the cask job executes.

mark-macos-arm64-release is always present when publish-cask runs: the job is needs-chained on publish, which is transitively downstream of sign — the uploader of that exact artifact — so a missing artifact already means a broken chain, and the new fail-closed existence check only converts an ambiguous selection into an explicit refusal.

sha256sum is the right digest tool for this ubuntu-latest job: it is the established tool in this workflow's ubuntu steps (prepare-publication's inventory hashing :1369, publish's bundle verification :1476); shasum is kept only where it already lives in macOS lanes.
